label: thm:jones-markov-trace
title: Existence and non-degeneracy of the Markov trace (Jones, 1987)
html:
Theorem. Existence and non-degeneracy of the Markov trace (Jones, 1987)

Let q \in \mathbb{C}^{\times} not be a root of unity. The Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(\mathbb{C}, q) admits a unique \mathbb{C}-linear functional \mathrm{tr}_M satisfying:

  1. Normalisation: \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1.
  2. Trace property: \mathrm{tr}_M(ab) = \mathrm{tr}_M(ba).
  3. Markov property, for x \in H_n(\mathbb{C}, q):
  \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x), \qquad
  z = \frac{q^3}{q^2 + 1} = \frac{q^2}{[2]_q} = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i)

the Markov-trace loop value — convention D of the trace-convention registry, the framework's production trace, with z(q_0) = 0.61268803714646525160. Earlier versions of this theorem wrote z = 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}), convention C, excised by the owner ruling of 2026-08-09. The two traces differ by 195.8 ppm on \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} and are not interchangeable. C is a Temperley–Lieb quantity attached to the wrong element and at the wrong argument: under the quadratic relation used here, \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + \mathbf{1}, the Temperley–Lieb generator is e_i := q - \sigma_i, with e_i^2 = [2]_q e_i, so the loop parameter is \delta = [2]_q = q + q^{-1} and not q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}. Convention D lands on the Jones–Temperley–Lieb normalisation exactly, \mathrm{tr}_M(e_i) = q - z = q/(q^2+1) = 1/[2]_q = 1/\delta (loop_reciprocal, TemperleyLiebTower.lean, sorry-free), while C assigned a loop reciprocal to the Hecke generator \sigma_i itself, and at x = q^{1/2} rather than x = q in 1/(x+x^{-1}) — the two differ by 0.408\,\%. The selection is forced rather than stipulated: see rem:markov-axioms-primitive.

For each partition \lambda \vdash n, the restriction of \mathrm{tr}_M to the irreducible H_n(\mathbb{C}, q)-module S_\lambda is the scalar multiple y_\lambda \chi_\lambda. Under convention D that scalar vanishes precisely when \ell(\lambda) \geq 3: the fibre V is the two-dimensional fundamental of \mathrm{SU}_q(2), so no partition with three or more rows survives Schur–Weyl, and \mathrm{tr}_M is faithful on the two-row stratum and on nothing else. The vanishing blocks span the radical of the trace form; the quotient is the Temperley–Lieb algebra, H_n(q)/\mathrm{rad} \cong \mathrm{TL}_n(q), and the surviving \sum \dim^2 is the Catalan number C_n — 2, 5, 14, 42, 132, 429 for n = 2, \ldots, 7 (TemperleyLiebTower.lean, sorry-free). The degeneracy is not a defect convention D introduced; it is what convention D means. For any braid \beta, \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho_n(\beta)) computes the Jones polynomial of the closure \hat{\beta} up to framing.
